doc.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023

title: Bandstand pet peeves: talking, dead time, warming up on stage, dress
summary: Vega lists what irritates him on the bandstand and how professionals should prepare and dress.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You try to tell your students about — well I’ll rephrase — is there anything on the bandstand that will aggravate you?

Yes. Talking on stage. Don’t talk on stage number one. Like the guy starts talking — you’re on a gig could you like not do that? That’s number one. Number two — talking on stage is a drag and talking between tunes is a major no-no. Like these kids will say, “Yeah I’m going to be playing at such-and-such a place, come out and see me.” So folks come out and they’re there and they play. They don’t come prepared. They don’t know what they’re going to play beforehand. They start calling tunes at that very moment. And this is a working group. “Let’s do this.” “Oh do you have that chart?” “Yeah.” No. Everything’s got to be — people are out, go from one thing to another. My thing is like have the music out, you finish, go to the next one. Don’t waste time. If there’s more than 30 seconds between tunes you’re wasting everybody’s time. You should be ready. You should be ready. So my thing is like I was trying out a new bass player yesterday so I told him, “Just get there a little early so that I could kind of get you into what we’re doing.” So I got there, I had music for him. “Here’s the charts.” I told him what the sequence of the tunes were. I might make a change but I told him always keep your music so you could make a quick change. It’s all good. It’s all good. Because the audience doesn’t want that. Hell no. The audience wants to go from one thing to another unless you’re going to speak to the audience. “Hi, how are you? Welcome. This is such-and-such.” But the musicians talking to each other, na. Another thing that’s a big no-no for me is a musician walking up on stage and deciding before they play that it’s time to warm up on stage. No. That’s a no-no. People don’t need to hear that shit. Sorry. You could take that out. They don’t need to hear that crap. Go to a stairway or something and do that. I don’t want to hear that. I don’t want to hear it. They don’t want to hear it. So you know respect your audience and don’t show up looking like a schlump. Don’t show up — I’m in New York so I’m going to say that. You know? Don’t look like a schlump. Go in there, you know, and you know don’t let the audience be better dressed than you are.
You’re defining what it is to be a professional.
